[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/4: [source_identity] ""That man was true"" vs "Καὶ ἦν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ἀληθινὸς": ἀληθινὸς means 'true/genuine' not 'true' in sense of truthful; 'that man' for ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος is acceptable; [completeness] ""Fear God, keep his commandments, for this is the whole of man"" vs "Τὸν Θεὸν φοβοῦ, τὰς ἐντολὰς φύλαττε, ὅτι τοῦτο πᾶς ἄνθρωπος": Missing ὅτι 'because/that'; 'whole of man' for πᾶς ἄνθρωπος is wrong—means 'every man' or 'all humankind'; [agency] ""He is blameless because he is righteous"" vs "Ἄμεμπτος, ἐπειδὴ δίκαιος": No explicit 'He is'; supplies subject and copula not in source; but meaning is clear; [completeness] ""He is God-fearing because a good life leads to the knowledge of God"" vs "Θεοσεβής, βίος γὰρ καλὸς τὸν Θεὸν ἐπιγνῶναι ποιεῖ": Missing explicit subject for Θεοσεβής; supplies 'He is' and 'leads to' for ποιεῖ 'makes/causes'; [scripture] "Chapter 1, verses 16 and 17" vs "ι΄, ιζ΄": Greek has 10, 17 not 16, 17—ι΄ = 10, not 16 (ιϛ΄); major verse reference error; [agency] ""He made the camels fall under the horsemen"" vs "Τὰς μὲν καμήλους πεποίηκε γενέσθαι ὑπὸ τοὺς ἱππεῖς": Subject is Satan/devil from context, but 'He' ambiguous; could mislead to God; [completeness] ""The donkeys and the oxen, the animals that plow and work the ground"" vs "τὰς ὀνάδας καὶ τοὺς βόας, τοὺς ἀροτριῶντας καὶ τὴν γῆν ἐργαζομένους": Adds 'the animals' not in source; participles directly modify the nouns; [agency] ""he brought down fire from heaven upon the sheep"" vs "πῦρ κατήγαγεν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ τὰ πρόβατα": Subject is Satan (from context), not God; 'he' ambiguous and potentially misleading; [scripture] "Chapter 2, verse 9" vs "Κεφ. Β΄, θ΄": Correct: Β΄ = 2, θ΄ = 9; [completeness] ""See the malice of it"" vs "Ὅρα τὸ κακοῦργον": 'of it' added; τὸ κακοῦργον is 'the malicious deed/act' or 'the villainy' | part 2/4: [source_identity] "Chapter 2, verse 9" vs "Κεφ. Ζʹ, αʹ": Greek has Chapter 7, 1; English invents Chapter 2 verse 9; [completeness] "See the malice of it: when much time had gone by, then she attacks" vs "τότε γὰρ μάλιστα...": Dropped entire interpretive clause about wife's malice and attack; not in Greek; [negation] "There is absolutely no one who does not worry" vs "Ἔστι δὲ ὅλως οὐδεὶς, ὃς οὐ τῶν ἀναγκαίων φροντίζει": Double negative flipped: Greek says 'there is no one who does not care' = all care; English same but 'absolutely' overstates οὐδεὶς...οὐ as intensifier rather than standard double negation; [agency] "I beg you to remember" vs "Ἱκετεύω δὴ μνησθῆναι": Greek has 'I beseech [impersonal/self]' not 'I beg you'; no second person object in source; [scripture] "Chapter 12, verse 5" vs "Κεφ. ΙΒʹ, εʹ": Greek has Chapter 12, 5 but LXX Job 12:5 is different; this matches Job 15:21 or similar, not 12:5 | part 3/4: [source_identity] ""He grows old like a wineskin"" vs "Ὃ παλαιοῦται": Relative pronoun 'which/what' not 'he'; subject is unspecified antecedent, not Job; [scripture] "Chapter 13, verse 28" vs "κηʹ": Greek has 28, but this is Job 13:28 in LXX; however Hebrew/English numbering differs—Job 13:28 in Hebrew is 13:27, but actually LXX Job 13:28 = Hebrew 13:28? Need verification: Hebrew Job has 13:28 as v.28, so this may be correct. Actually checking: MT Job 13:28 has 28 verses, so LXX 13:28 = MT 13:28. But the citation format should show Hebrew/English if different. Uncertain on this—actually MT Job 13 has 28 verses, so numbering matches. No defect. | part 4/4: [completeness] ""He does not say these things according to his own wish"" vs "Οὐ κατὰ βούλησιν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ταῦτα λέγει": Missing "τὴν ἑαυτοῦ" = "his own"; "wish" for βούλησιν is acceptable; [completeness] ""and will not stand"" vs "καὶ οὐ μὴ στῇ": Dropped double negative οὐ μὴ = "by no means shall he stand" / "he shall not stand" (emphatic); [completeness] ""he leaves no remembrance among the living"" vs "οὐδὲ μνημόσυνόν τι τοῖς ζῶσιν ἀφίησιν": Dropped "τι" = "any" ("not even any memorial"); [negation] ""not even any memorial" vs "no remembrance"" vs "οὐδὲ μνημόσυνόν τι": οὐδὲ = "not even" (adversative/emphatic), not simple "no"; this is borderline but acceptable; [completeness] ""but by the word of God"" vs "ἀλλ' ἐκ ῥήσεως Θεοῦ": "utterance" or "saying" for ῥήσεως is more precise than "word"; acceptable synonym; [completeness] ""and no one goes beyond"" vs "οὐχ ὑπερβαίνοντος τὸν παρ' αὐτοῦ τεταγμένον βίον": Participial construction "[God] not going beyond" rendered as finite clause with "no one"; acceptable restructuring; [completeness] ""These things must not be said"" vs "Ταῦτα δὲ οὐχ... λεκτέον": Missing "δὲ" = "then/therefore"; dropped connective; [completeness] ""as if fate rules"" vs "ὡς εἱμαρμένης κρατούσης": "fate" for εἱμαρμένης acceptable; "rules" for genitive absolute participle acceptable; [completeness] ""but as the will of God arranging each thing by bounds and measures"" vs "ἀλλ' ὡς τοῦ θελήματος τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅροις καὶ μέτροις ἕκαστα διαταξαμένου": Missing "τοῦ" before θελήματος = "of-the"; participial construction obscured; [completeness] ""What? Were you born the first of human beings?"" vs "Τί γάρ; μὴ πρῶτος ἀνθρώπων ἐγεννήθης;": Missing "γάρ" = "for"; "What?" for "Τί γάρ;" weakens the rhetorical force; [completeness] ""Or were you formed before the hills?"" vs "ἢ πρὸ θινῶν ἐπάγης;": "formed" for ἐπάγης (2nd sing. aor. pass. of πήγνυμι) = "were you fixed/established"; acceptable; [completeness] ""Or have you heard the ordinance of the Lord?"" vs "ἢ σύνταγμα Κυρίου ἀκήκοας;": "ordinance" for σύνταγμα acceptable; "Lord" for Κυρίου acceptable; [completeness] ""This means: Did you exist before all human beings"" vs "Ἀντὶ τοῦ· μὴ πρὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων ὑπέστης": "This means" for Ἀντὶ τοῦ = "Instead of this" / "In place of this"; acceptable paraphrase; [completeness] ""and have you stretched out your life until now"" vs "καὶ ἄχρι τοῦ νῦν διατείνας τὸν βίον": Participial construction "having stretched out" rendered as finite verb; acceptable; [completeness] ""so that you have had experience of more things than those of the same nature as you?"" vs "πλειόνων πραγμάτων πεῖραν ἔσχηκας παρὰ τοὺς ὁμοφυεῖς": Missing explicit "so that" in source; added interpretation; [completeness] ""Where is the high and hard-to-reach place, or the sandy one?"" vs "Ἵνα ἐστὶν ὁ ὑψηλὸς τόπος καὶ δύσβατος, ἤτοι ψαμμώδης": "Where is" for Ἵνα ἐστὶν = "Where is"; but ἵνα normally = "in order that" — here interrogative ἵνα is rare; acceptable as Theodotion's reading; [completeness] ""The Hebrew: 'You were conceived.'"" vs "Ὁ Ἑβραῖος· Συνελήφθης": Missing article: "The Hebrew [version/reading]"; acceptable
[glm @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 4/4: [completeness] "everyone who is afflicted suffers these things because he has sinned" vs "πᾶς θλιβόμενος ἁμαρτὼν ταῦτα ὑφίσταται": ἁμαρτών is a genitive plural noun 'of sins', not 'because he has sinned'; causal sense is interpretive.; [source_identity] "Or were you formed before the hills?" vs "ἢ πρὸ θινῶν ἐπάγης;": ἐπάγης means 'were you placed/set', not 'were you formed'; different verb than πλασθῆναι.

ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I checked each flag against the Greek and found no meaning error. 'Chapter 1, verses 16 and 17' is right by content: Πῦρ ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (Job 1:16) and the camels taken captive (1:17). The printed 'ι ʹ, ιζʹ' is a misprint for ιϛʹ, ιζʹ. 'Chapter 2, verse 9' introduces Χρόνου δὲ πολλοῦ προβεβηκότος, εἶπεν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ, and the Greek prints Κεφ. Βʹ, θʹ before it; 'Κεφ. Ζʹ, αʹ' belongs to the following lemma. The malice clause (Ὅρα τὸ κακοῦργον …) is in the Greek. Job 12:5 LXX is ἡτοιμάσθαι πεσεῖν ὑπὸ ἄλλους εἰς χρόνον τακτόν, as quoted. 'For this is the whole of man' is the standard rendering of Eccl 12:13 τοῦτο πᾶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος. 'He' in the camels sentence is the devil, as the context makes clear. The rest (double negatives, 'I beg you', supplied copulas) is idiom.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), clause-by-clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): I found no meaning error. ἁμαρτών is the aorist participle of ἁμαρτάνω ('having sinned'), not a genitive plural noun (which would be ἁμαρτιῶν), so 'because he has sinned' is right. 'Were you formed' for ἐπάγης (πήγνυμι, 'were you fixed/established') keeps the sense of Job 15:7.
